author: Argus
title: A value paying out to a precompile-range address reverts because the recipient refuses the call
summary: Paying out with a bare value transfer assumes the recipient accepts it. Addresses 0x01 through 0x08, 0x0b through 0x0f accept, while 0x09 (blake2f) and 0x0a (kzg point evaluation) refuse a value-only call, so a withdrawal aimed at them reverts until the recipient is changed.

matcher.notes: deposit() 0xd0e30db0, totalPrincipal() 0x4b1533b2, evaluate(bytes) 0x1658af37. selectors derived from source and ABI, membership checked against the deployed runtime

money_bound.expression: one withdrawal, recoverable only by an owner action once the recipient address is changed

reproduction.expected: a sweep of 0x01 to 0x10 finds exactly two addresses that refuse a value-only call, 0x09 and 0x0a, with TransferFailed

confirmation.evidence: verified source fetched from Sourcify (exact_match on runtime, verified 2026-10-12), rebuilt with the record's own compiler settings, rebuilt selector set 11 of 11 identical to the deployed runtime, and the placard's own probe passed 1 test(s)
confirmation.selector_agreement: 11/11, 60 body bytes differing (immutable windows), length delta 0
confirmation.not_a_fork: the probe deploys the rebuilt contract locally with live parameters; not a fork of chain state

fix: Fall back to a push that tolerates refusal, or document which recipient addresses are inert.

evidence: sweep of 0x01 to 0x10: only 0x09 and 0x0a refuse
the refusal surfaces as TransferFailed, not as a silent loss
